concepts.label: XDCR Advanced Filtering
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - this is the Web Console procedure guide's own step-by-step page for the promoted concept

concepts.label: XDCR deletion filter
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a family of three checkboxes ('Do not replicate document expirations', 'Do not replicate DELETE operations', 'Remove TTL from replicated items') controlling whether a source-side deletion/expiration/TTL propagates to the replicated copy, independent of and orthogonal to the regular-expression/SQL++ filtering-expression mechanism. First contact anywhere in the corpus - the reference tree's xdcr-filtering-reference-intro.md/xdcr-filtering-expressions.md (round 20) document only the match-expression side of filtering and never mention deletion propagation at all, a genuinely UI-procedure-only mechanism this batch's brief predicted.

concepts.label: XDCR explicit mapping (collection-to-collection)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - an administrator-specified rule remapping a source keyspace to a differently-named target keyspace, as against the default xdcr:implicit-mapping (minted on create-xdcr-replication.json, this same batch). First genuine use on this page's CLI example ('This also requires an _explicit mapping_ to be specified'); the concept's fuller defining prose is on replicate-using-scopes-and-collections.md, this same batch, reused there.

relations.subject: xdcr:replication-filter
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (restrictedToContext) - a length restriction that applies only via the UI access surface, not the CLI or REST API
relations.evidence: Note that when entered by means of the [UI](#filter-an-xdcr-replication-with-the-ui), the expression can be a maximum of 250 bytes (characters) in length: this restriction does _not_ apply to expressions entered by means of the [CLI](#filter-an-xdcr-replication-with-the-cli) or the [REST API](#filter-an-xdcr-replication-with-the-rest-api).

relations.subject: xdcr:replication-filter
relations.object: more than one filter per replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (doesNotSupport) - object is a described restriction, not a concept id
relations.evidence: Only one filter can be applied to a single replication: thus, once defined, the filter is applied to _all_ mappings.

relations.subject: xdcr:replication
relations.object: more than one replication per target bucket
relations.evidence: Note also that only _one_ replication can be established between a given source bucket and a given target bucket.

relations.subject: xdcr:deletion-filter
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (doesNotAffect) - the two filtering mechanisms operate independently of each other
relations.evidence: Note that the replication of deletions, expirations, and/or TTLs is _not_ prevented by the specifying of a filter that is formed with regular and other filtering expressions: to ensure that document-deletions, expirations, and/or TTLs are _not_ replicated, the appropriate deletion-filter checkboxes must be checked.

relations.subject: xdcr:deletion-filter
relations.evidence: **Remove TTL from replicated items**. If checked, this means that the TTL that a document bears at source is _not_ made part of the replicated copy of the document: instead, the TTL of the replicated copy is set to 0.

relations.subject: xdcr:replication-filter
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresPriorExecutionOf) - object is a described action, not a concept id
relations.evidence: Note that an expression _must_ be tested successfully, before it can be included as part of the replication: if an expression is specified and attemptedly saved without having been tested, the expression is ignored when saving occurs; and the replication is thus started in unfiltered form.

relations.subject: xdcr:replication-filter
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted concept reused loosely: no version:server-7-1-5 concept file was confirmed at extraction time (see this batch's own version:server-7-1 note on create-xdcr-replication.json for the same near-miss); flagged for reconciliation rather than silently rounded
relations.evidence: The behavior is identical to that of Couchbase-Server versions prior to 7.1.5, where the option did not exist.
